record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Develop the theory of Bose-Einstein condensation, either as part of the fermionic BCS program where the bosons are Cooper pairs or as an independent bosonic constructive program.

evidence.quote: Develop the theory of Bose-Einstein condensation. This can be viewed as a piece of the previous BCS program where the bosons are Cooper pairs

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Within the framework of constructive quantum field theory, develop a mathematically rigorous theory of Bose–Einstein condensation for an interacting many-body system. Concretely, accomplish at least one of the following two programs.

(A) Fermionic (BCS) route. Consider a system of nonrelativistic spin-1/2 fermions in d-dimensional Euclidean space (d = 2 or 3) at positive density and low temperature, with a translation-invariant short-range two-body attractive interaction, described by a grand-canonical Hamiltonian
  H = ∫ ψ*_σ(x)(−Δ−μ)ψ_σ(x) dx + ∫∫ V(x−y) ψ*_↑(x)ψ*_↓(y)ψ_↓(y)ψ_↑(x) dx dy.
Starting from the corresponding Euclidean functional integral, construct (with full control of the thermodynamic limit, ultraviolet/infrared regularizations, and convergence of the perturbation expansion, e.g. via multiscale/cluster/renormalization-group methods) a phase exhibiting a nonzero condensate of Cooper pairs, i.e. prove that the two-point pair correlation
  ⟨ψ_↑(x)ψ_↓(y)⟩
has a nonzero limit as |x−y| → ∞ in a suitable low-temperature regime, accompanied by spontaneous breaking of the global U(1) particle-number symmetry and the existence of a gapless Goldstone mode.

(B) Independent bosonic route. Consider an interacting bosonic field — for instance a non-relativistic Bose gas with repulsive pair interaction V ≥ 0 of finite range, or a Euclidean |φ|^4 complex scalar theory in d ≥ 3 dimensions — and construct, by a constructive (non-perturbative) procedure, an infinite-volume Gibbs/Euclidean state in which the U(1) symmetry is spontaneously broken: ⟨φ(x)⟩ ≠ 0, equivalently the one-particle reduced density matrix has a macroscopic eigenvalue. Establish existence of the corresponding infinite-volume measure, exponential clustering of truncated correlations of massive modes, and a Goldstone (gapless) mode associated with the broken symmetry.

The task is to carry out either (A) or (B) with mathematically rigorous, non-perturbative control, thereby providing a constructive field-theoretic proof of Bose–Einstein condensation in an interacting system.
artifact.category_tag: Constructive quantum field theory and Bose-Einstein condensation
artifact.status_search_result: Rigorous BEC has been proved for interacting dilute Bose gases in special scaling regimes (Gross–Pitaevskii limit, mean-field limit, and at positive temperature in traps), and algebraic/perturbative constructions exist for relativistic |φ|^4 condensates. However, a full constructive field-theory proof of BEC for a translation-invariant interacting boson system in the thermodynamic limit at fixed density, or a constructive treatment of Cooper-pair condensation in the BCS program, remains open.

status_evidence.title: Bose–Einstein Condensation in a Dilute, Trapped Gas at Positive Temperature
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorous proof of BEC for interacting dilute Bose gas in the Gross–Pitaevskii limit at positive temperature in a trap.
status_evidence.claim: BEC is proved rigorously only in specific scaling/trap regimes, not in the full constructive thermodynamic-limit setting.

status_evidence.title: Algebraic Approach to Bose–Einstein Condensation in Relativistic QFT
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs BEC states for relativistic complex scalar field with |φ|^4 interaction perturbatively over a classical condensate.
status_evidence.claim: Existing constructions are perturbative around a classical condensate rather than fully non-perturbative constructive QFT results.
